newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Alfa Group mulls $50 mln Cuba sugar credit.
newsitem.headline: Russian Alfa Group mulls $50 mln Cuba sugar credit.

text.p: Alfa Group, one of Russia's biggest importers of Cuban raw sugar, is considering extending a credit of up to $50 million to Cuba to help finance the 1998 sugar cane harvest, Itar-Tass news agency said on Thursday.
Tass quoted a spokesman from Alfa Group's foreign relations department as saying Alfa Group planned to import 300,000 tonnes of Cuban raw sugar to June.
The company plans a syndicated credit offered jointly with a number of Western banks.
The spokesman said the number of banks and the amount of the investment had not been determined yet, but the credit would be over $25 million.
It would be the first ever Russian investment in Cuban sugar production despite the long-time partnership between the two countries, Tass said.

The group's Alfa-Eko unit recently told Reuters it would not participate in new sugar-for-oil deals, a barter trading system which is the primary form of sugar trade with Cuba and has been in place since Soviet times.
